newsitem.title: MEXICO: Bufete preparing big refinery bid -analysts.
newsitem.headline: Bufete preparing big refinery bid -analysts.

text.p: Mexican construction company Bufete Industrial has joined powerful allies to bid for the expansion of a crude refinery, but analysts say it will have to learn from past mistakes to win the competitive $1.2 billion construction project.

On Tuesday, Bufete said it would form a consortium with Japanese powerhouses Mitsubishi Corp, Mitsui & Co. Ltd. and Itochu Corp to bid for the Cadereyta refinery expansion and renovation close to this industrial city in northern Mexico.
"It is very clear why they joined with the Japanese -- because of the yen financing," UBS Securities construction analyst Alvaro Shiraishi said.
He added, however, that Bufete's alliance with Mitsui and Shell Oil for the Merida III natural gas pipeline earlier this year was unsuccessful.
"The thing that wins these bids is the economic proposal, and for Bufete, it will be very difficult to convince three Japanese companies to lower their profit margins for the project," he added.
Bids for the refinery are expected to be opened by August, with a decision due in the following months.
The project is part of a key expansion strategy to Mexico's refining output by state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).
More than ten different companies are known to be bidding for the three-year project, and analysts said they expect alliances will be formed to strengthen competitive positions.

Analysts have said a high proposed construction cost for the Merida III pipeline may have cost Bufete, Mitsui and Shell the project. Winning bidders TransCanada Pipelines Ltd, U.S. International Generating Co. and private Mexican builder Gutsa Construcciones expect to spend $240 million on the project.

"The association with the Japaneses for Cadereyta does not give Bufete an advantage unless Mitsui learned from the Merida disappointment and lowered their margins," Hector Castillo, ING Barings construction analyst in New York, told Reuters. Analysts
have said that Bufete's low backlog is the company's principal short term risk, but that a project such as Cadereyta could be the company's key income base for the next few years.
